postings.title: Advanced Technology Engineer
postings.description:
GomSpace
Advanced Technology Engineer
Shape the future of space missions from concept to orbit
We are seeking an experienced Advanced Technology Engineer to lead mission design and system architecture development for small satellite missions. In this role, you will drive early-phase technical decision-making through orbit analysis, payload accommodation, communications link design, and end-to-end mission configuration — while pioneering advanced engineering methods including AI-enabled tools and digital engineering techniques.
You will join our Advanced Missions team, working at the front end of space programs where mission success begins with innovative concepts, rigorous trade-offs, and forward-looking technology.
Your Role
As Advanced Technology Engineer, you will lead mission architecture development and system-level trade studies that guide GomSpace's most ambitious proposals. You will use mature and advanced engineering methods and apply them to real mission challenges across sovereign, defence, and institutional programmes.
Your key responsibilities include:
Lead mission design and system architecture development, including orbit analysis, payload accommodation, navigation concepts, communications links, and end-to-end mission configurations.
Perform system-level trade-offs and comparative mission analyses to guide early-phase technical decision-making.
Evaluate and mature advanced engineering methods, including AI-enabled tools, automation frameworks, and novel modelling or simulation techniques.
Support project execution by providing mission trade-offs, refining architectures as constraints evolve, and ensuring feasibility, robustness, and performance throughout the lifecycle.
Drive proposal development and innovation, contributing mission concepts, trade studies, and value propositions while scouting and applying new techniques such as AI/ML optimisation, hybrid simulation, design-space exploration, and digital engineering tools.
What Success Looks Like
In the initial phase, success means:
Integrating into the Advanced Mission BU and establishing working relationships with engineering teams in Aalborg.
Delivering your first mission architecture trade study and contributing to at least one active proposal.
Demonstrating clear and effective communication of trade-off results to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Over time, you will be recognised for establishing and maintaining a reusable mission design toolchain — including AI/ML-enabled methods — and for leading end-to-end mission design that strengthens GomSpace's competitive position in institutional and defence markets.
What You Bring
You are a mission designer and systems architect with strong experience in early-phase spacecraft mission development, comfortable working at the intersection of technical depth and strategic decision-making.
You likely bring:
An MSc or PhD in Aerospace/Systems Engineering, Astrodynamics, or a related field.
3–5+ years of experience in mission design, system architecture, or spacecraft systems engineering.
Experience with orbit analysis, link budgets, payload accommodation, and trade studies.
Proficiency in mission analysis tools (STK, GMAT, or similar).
Familiarity with AI/ML techniques, automation frameworks, or digital engineering tools.
Experience with proposal writing and bid support is a strong plus.
Exposure to ESA/ECSS project lifecycle phases is highly valued.
Who You Are
You bring clarity to early-phase ambiguity and rigour to complex trade-offs. You are analytical, creative, and driven by the challenge of turning mission concepts into viable architectures.
You are known for:
Customer focus – ensuring focus on customer’s success.
Execution discipline – ensuring commitments are met in demanding environments.
Curiosity and initiative — actively scouting and applying new methods to push the boundaries of mission design.
Analytical depth — combining strong technical fundamentals with creative problem-solving.
Collaborative communication — bridging technical complexity with stakeholder needs.
True leadership — taking ownership of your domain and acting with integrity.
Comfort with ambiguity — thriving in early-phase environments where requirements evolve and decisions shape outcomes.
Why Join Us
You will play a key role in shaping future space missions at their most decisive stage. This position offers the opportunity to work closely with leading institutional customers, influence mission architectures from the start, and contribute to programs with long-term strategic impact.

postings.title: AOCS Engineer – Shape Orbits, Guide Missions, and Bring Space to Life
postings.description:
GomSpace
AOCS Engineer – Shape Orbits, Guide Missions, and Bring Space to Life
Are you an AOCS engineer who dreams of building systems that keep satellites steady, precise, and mission-ready as they orbit Earth?
Do you find inspiration in transforming equations, algorithms, and hardware into technologies that silently guide spacecraft through the darkness of space?
At GomSpace, we make space yours — one mission at a time.
Our satellites deliver impact that reaches far beyond Earth’s orbit — turning space into opportunity, mission by mission. If you want to join a company where ambition meets precision, and where your work truly leaves Earth, this is your chance.
Your Role
You’ll work at the very core of spacecraft capability: how a satellite understands itself, stabilizes, maneuvers, and performs on orbit. Depending on your strengths and interests, you’ll join either our Products Business Unit, where you help shape and refine the AOCS technologies powering our satellite platforms, or our Programs Business Unit, where you contribute to full missions from concept to launch and beyond.
Your work will bridge analytical modeling with hands-on engineering. You’ll simulate spacecraft dynamics, design control strategies, develop software that must perform flawlessly in orbit, refine our AOCS architectures, and support real spacecraft in our cleanroom — and eventually in space.
You’ll collaborate with mission teams, Systems Engineering, and customers to ensure every spacecraft we build performs precisely as intended when it matters most.
Your tasks include:
• Designing AOCS solutions and integrating/testing components and algorithms
• Engaging with customers to understand requirements and align on mission-ready solutions
• Selecting and evaluating attitude determination sensors and actuators
• Developing simulations and software in MATLAB, Simulink, C, and C++
• Supporting integration, testing, and troubleshooting in the cleanroom and, when needed, in orbit
Short- and Long-Term Success
In the initial phase, success means:
• Delivering high-quality AOCS analyses, simulations, and software that advance mission performance
• Supporting spacecraft integration and testing with accuracy and confidence
• Building trust and strong technical relationships with customers and internal teams
Longer term, you’ll take ownership of AOCS architecture evolution, contribute to next-generation pointing and control solutions, and help shape the capabilities of the next wave of GOMSPACE spacecraft — systems that will orbit Earth for years to come.
What You Bring
You’re a technically strong engineer who finds purpose in building systems that behave reliably in the unforgiving environment of space. You’re motivated by the elegance of control theory, the challenge of spacecraft dynamics, and the satisfaction of turning physics and code into something that can fly.
You value precision. You appreciate the art and discipline behind creating something that must operate without hesitation, correction, or compromise hundreds of kilometers above Earth. And you take pride in building solutions that last.
You likely:
• Hold a degree in Control & Automation or a related field (MSc or higher preferred)
• Understand key AOCS components such as IMUs, star trackers, reaction wheels, and RCS
• Have programming experience in C, C++, Python, MATLAB, or similar
• Are confident working with Linux-based systems
• Communicate clearly and can explain complex systems in simple, understandable language
Who You Are
You’re not just an engineer — you’re someone who wants to see the systems you build operate in orbit, where precision is everything and where engineering transforms into something almost poetic. You’re curious, rigorous, collaborative, and driven by the feeling of seeing a spacecraft you helped create perform flawlessly above our planet.
You bring:
• Helpfulness – you support teammates and customers with expertise and empathy
• Open communication – you’re transparent, proactive, and always follow up
• True leadership – you take ownership, act with integrity, and deliver on commitments
• Structure & clarity – you enjoy building and maintaining scalable engineering processes
• Human insight – you understand how your work affects missions, people, and critical decisions
You’re motivated by creating solutions that survive the extremes of space — and by the discipline required to make that possible.
Why Join Us?
At GomSpace, you won’t just work on a product — you’ll help create spacecraft that orbit Earth, expand knowledge, connect people, and open new possibilities far beyond our atmosphere.
We believe innovation thrives when talented people are trusted, supported, and inspired to push boundaries together. Here, your work will matter — to missions, to partners, and to the long-term evolution of space technology.
Here’s why you’ll love working with us:
• Be part of a global company making a real impact in the space industry
• Get freedom under responsibility from day one — and grow with us
• Join a dynamic, full-service environment where no two days are alike
• Work across borders and build a strong international network
• Be part of a culture where collaboration beats competition — and milestones are celebrated together

postings.title: AOCS/GNC Engineer
postings.description:
GomSpace
AOCS/GNC Engineer
Design the systems that guide satellites in orbit for new ambitious missions
We are seeking an experienced AOCS/GNC Engineer to design, develop, and validate attitude determination, orbit control, and autonomous navigation solutions for small satellite missions. In this role, you will develop guidance and control strategies across diverse and demanding mission profiles — from VLEO drag-dominated regimes to deep-space trajectories and asteroid proximity operations.
You will join our Advanced Missions global team, developing next-generation AOCS/GNC concepts while collaborating closely with GomSpace's established AOCS team in Aalborg — who built and flew the AOCS for the Juventas CubeSat on ESA's Hera mission and are currently developing full 6-DoF GNC for the Llevant (RAMSES) asteroid rendezvous mission.
Your Role
As AOCS/GNC Engineer, you will own the attitude and orbit control design for advanced mission proposals — from requirements definition and algorithm design through high-fidelity simulation and hardware-in-the-loop validation.
Your key responsibilities include:
Design and implement AOCS/GNC algorithms for attitude determination, control, and autonomous navigation across diverse mission profiles.
Develop guidance and orbit-control strategies tailored to SSA, VLEO drag-dominated regimes, and deep-space trajectories.
Model and simulate spacecraft dynamics, environmental disturbances, and sensor/actuator performance for mission-specific scenarios.
Validate algorithms through high-fidelity simulations, Monte-Carlo analyses, and hardware-in-the-loop setups.
Collaborate with systems, propulsion, and mission design teams to define control requirements and ensure end-to-end stability and performance.
What Success Looks Like
In the initial phase, success means:
Understanding GomSpace's AOCS product portfolio (GSW-600 reaction wheels, Auriga/Twinkle star trackers, STIM300 IMU, AOCS Flightcore software).
Delivering your first AOCS sizing and mode analysis for a mission proposal and setting up a reusable MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment.
Establishing working relationships with the Aalborg AOCS team and communicating AOCS trade-offs clearly to non-AOCS stakeholders.
Over time, you will be recognised for owning end-to-end AOCS/GNC design for advanced mission proposals, developing and maintaining GNC strategies across multiple mission regimes, and achieving successful Monte-Carlo validation campaigns that demonstrate algorithm robustness.
What You Bring
You are an AOCS/GNC specialist with deep analytical rigour and a passion for solving complex spacecraft dynamics and control challenges across unconventional mission profiles.
You likely bring:
An MSc or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, Astrodynamics, Control Systems, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. A PhD focused on GNC, spacecraft dynamics, or autonomous navigation is a strong plus.
3–5+ years of experience in AOCS/GNC algorithm design, simulation, and validation for spacecraft missions.
Experience with attitude determination (gyro-stellar estimators, EKF/UKF), 3-axis control (sliding mode, PD/PID, LQR), and momentum management.
Proficiency in MATLAB/Simulink for spacecraft dynamics modelling and Monte-Carlo analysis.
Experience with C/C++ implementation of flight algorithms and familiarity with AOCS sensors and actuators (star trackers, IMUs, reaction wheels, magnetorquers, RCS thrusters).
Exposure to ESA/ECSS project lifecycle and AOCS design reviews (PDR, CDR) is highly valued.
Who You Are
You combine deep mathematical rigour with creative engineering intuition. You are energised by the challenge of designing control solutions for missions that push the boundaries of what nanosatellites can do.
You are known for:
Analytical depth — AOCS/GNC demands mathematical precision, and you deliver it.
Creative problem solving — developing novel control strategies for unconventional mission profiles.
Collaborative communication — translating complex dynamics and control concepts into clear requirements for systems and propulsion teams.
Self-driven initiative — comfortable with ambiguity in early-phase mission design.
Execution discipline – ensuring commitments are met in demanding environments.
Customer focus – ensuring focus on customer’s success.

Experienced Hardware Engineer: Lead the integration of the hardware that powers ambitious satellite missions
We are seeking an experienced Hardware Engineer to drive the integration, technical ownership, and continuous improvement of the hardware platforms that enable GomSpace's satellite missions.

Experienced Systems Engineer – Architecting Nanosatellite & Microsatellite Systems (DK/LU)
Do you want to own the technical integrity of a mission from "blank sheet" to flight-ready hardware?

RF Subsystems Engineer - Design the communication systems that connect ambitious satellite missions to Earth
We are seeking an experienced RF Subsystems Engineer to design, develop, and validate RF communication subsystems for ambitious nanosatellite missions.
In this role, you will design and integrate RF front-end components across UHF, S-band, and X-band systems, perform link budget analyses, and validate performance through hardware-in-the-loop and over-the-air testing.
You will join our Advanced Missions global team, working on next-generation RF concepts and mission-specific communication architectures while collaborating closely with GomSpace’s RF Hardware team in Aalborg — whose flight-proven NanoCom radios and SDR platform are on orbit today across missions like GOMX-4, GOMX-5, Starling, and Juventas (ESA/Hera). Depending on the mission, you may contribute to conventional communication subsystems, software-defined radio applications, or advanced RF sensing payloads.
Important eligibility requirement: Employment in this position requires eligibility for national and EU security clearance. Certain citizenships or dual citizenships may affect the ability to obtain such clearance under applicable regulations.
Your Role
As RF Subsystems Engineer, you will own the end-to-end RF subsystem architecture for advanced mission proposals, from link budget analysis and front-end design through firmware development, HIL testing, and over-the-air validation.
Your key responsibilities include:
Define RF subsystem architectures and perform trade-offs across frequency bands, performance, and constraints
Perform link budget analysis, RF chain modelling, and system-level performance optimisation
Specify RF subsystem requirements and interfaces in coordination with system and payload teams
Support integration, verification, and validation of RF subsystems, including HIL and over-the-air testing
Contribute to selection and oversight of RF front-end components and suppliers (UHF/VHF/S/X-band)
Identify and assess onboard signal processing and data reduction algorithms for RF payloads.
Assess radar emitter detection, classification, and geolocation techniques using pulse and spectral analysis.
What Success Looks Like
In the initial phase, success means:
Understanding GomSpace’s NanoCom product portfolio and SDR architecture.
Completing a link budget analysis for an active mission proposal and performing your first HIL or over-the-air RF test using GomSpace equipment.
Communicating RF trade-offs and link budget results clearly to non-RF stakeholders.
Contributing directly to winning new mission opportunities through robust RF subsystem designs and credible technical proposals.
Over time, you will be recognised for owning end-to-end RF subsystem design for mission proposals — from link budget through component selection to test verification — and for establishing reusable RF modelling and simulation tools for the BU.
What You Bring
You are an RF engineer with hands-on experience in satellite communication systems, comfortable moving between simulation, the lab bench, and system-level integration.
You likely bring:
An MSc or PhD in Electrical Engineering, RF/Microwave Engineering, Telecommunications, or a related field.
5+ years of experience in RF subsystem design, testing, or integration for satellite or aerospace applications.
Hands-on experience with UHF, S-band, or X-band communication systems.
Proficiency in RF simulation and design tools (CST, ADS, HFSS, or similar) and experience with spectrum analysers, VNAs, and RF test equipment.
Familiarity with modulation schemes (GMSK, QPSK, 8PSK, DVB-S2) and communication protocols (CSP, CCSDS).
Experience in RF payload design, digital signal processing (DSP), or sensing systems would be considered a strong advantage.
Experience with RF signal analysis and/or ELINT/SIGINT techniques (e.g. radar pulse detection, classification, and geolocation).
Experience with ECSS standards or space-grade RF qualification is a strong plus.
Who You Are
You are precise, methodical, and energised by the challenge of squeezing maximum performance out of tight RF margins in space. You enjoy the full cycle — from modelling a link budget to measuring real hardware on the bench.
You are known for:
Precision and attention to detail — RF performance in space demands it.
Hands-on problem solving — equally comfortable in simulation tools and at the lab bench.
Collaborative communication — able to bridge RF-specific topics with systems and payload teams.
Curiosity — eager to explore emerging RF technologies and push boundaries in nanosatellite communications.
Execution discipline — delivering results in demanding, schedule-driven environments.
Customer focus – ensuring focus on customer’s success.
True leadership — taking ownership of your domain and driving technical excellence.
Why Join Us
